chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Yunus ibn Ya'qub said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'I led a group in prayer, sat for the Tashahhud, then stood up and forgot to greet them (with Salam).' They said: 'You did not greet usaid: 'You did not greet us.' He said: 'Did you not greet while you were sitting?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then there is no blame on you. And if you had forgotten when they told you, you should have faced them with your face and said: Peace be upon you.'

key_terms.أُسَلِّمَ: To give the greeting of peace (Salam) to conclude prayer
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: The sitting portion of the prayer where testimonies are recited

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a prayer leader forgets to say Salam to the congregation after standing up?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for the *ma'mum* (congregant) who forgets the final *Salam* after rising, establishing that the initial greeting while seated suffices. Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a practical remedy—facing the congregation and verbally greeting them—highlighting the Shia emphasis on ease (*yusr*) and avoiding unnecessary complexity in acts of worship. This ruling underscores the distinction between the obligatory nature of the greeting and the flexibility granted for unintentional omissions during congregational prayer.
